antigens.title: #41 Off-by-one in slice end
antigens.pattern: Using slice(start, start + n - 1) instead of slice(start, start + n), dropping the last item of every page because slice's end index is already exclusive

code.explain: slice() call whose end argument is reduced by 1 — the end index is already exclusive, so this drops the last element

signatures.fix_hint: The end index of slice() is exclusive, so use slice(start, start + size) with no - 1.
signatures.antibody: test('regression #41: full pages keep their last item', () => { assert.deepEqual(page([1,2,3,4,5], 0, 2), [1,2]); assert.deepEqual(page([1,2,3,4,5], 2, 2), [5]); });

patches.explain: drop the '- 1': slice()'s end index is already exclusive (the #41 fix)

antigens.title: #57 Missing null guard on nested customer field
antigens.pattern: Reading a nested object property (e.g. customer.address.city) without an optional-chaining guard, crashing when the intermediate object is undefined or null
unfinished_followups: Add a regression test for customers with no address
Audit other code that reads nested customer fields

code.explain: two-level property access on customer object without optional chaining — crashes if the intermediate object is undefined

signatures.fix_hint: Guard the nested object with ?. (the #57 fix); add a sensible default if the caller needs one.
signatures.antibody: test('regression #57: billingCity survives no address', () => { assert.equal(billingCity({}), 'Unknown'); assert.equal(billingCity({address: {city: 'NYC'}}), 'NYC'); });

patches.explain: guard the nested object with ?. (the #57 fix); add a sensible default if the caller needs one

antigens.title: #63 Float money math
antigens.pattern: Summing currency values as IEEE 754 floating-point numbers, causing rounding drift (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3); fix is to work in integer cents

code.explain: reduce() accumulating a money field via direct property access (lowercase var.field, not Math.round) — float sum without integer-cent conversion

signatures.fix_hint: Sum in integer cents and divide once (the #63 fix).

example.before: return lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.price * l.qty, 0);
example.after:
const cents = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + Math.round(l.price * 100) * l.qty, 0);
  return cents / 100;

signatures.antibody: test('regression #63: no float drift', () => { assert.equal(invoiceTotal([{price: 0.1, qty: 1}, {price: 0.2, qty: 1}]), 0.3); });

patches.replace: const cents = \1.reduce((sum, \2) => sum + Math.round(\2.\3 * 100) * \2.\4, 0); return cents / 100
patches.explain: sum in integer cents and divide once (the #63 fix)

patches.replace: const cents = \1.reduce((sum, \2) => sum + Math.round(\2.\3 * 100), 0); return cents / 100
patches.explain: sum in integer cents and divide once (the #63 fix) — single-field variant
